description:
Problem: the verdict job grants id-token: write job-wide (.github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml:69-73), so ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN and _URL are in the environment of every run step, including the attempt loop that starts the reviewer. Yama ptrace_scope 1 blocks /proc/<pid>/mem but not /proc/<pid>/environ, which needs only READ mode for a same-user process (security/yama/yama_lsm.c checks PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH only; fs/proc/base.c environ_open uses PTRACE_MODE_READ). actions/runner sets the request token to the same value as ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN (ScriptHandler.cs:318, NodeScriptActionHandler.cs:57,69), so a leak grants Actions service access for the job's lifetime. Redaction matches only literal or control-split values, so any encoding defeats it. The 2026-10-25 single-job decision record accepted this risk because the value is redacted; that premise is false.

Outcome (owner D2): the tailscale/github-action step authenticates with oauth-client-id and oauth-secret from the oracle environment secrets TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID and TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET (tags tag:oracle-ci); the job drops id-token: write; the OAuth secret appears only in that step; HAS_TAILNET is built from TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID and TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET and the workflow names neither TS_AUDIENCE nor TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID anywhere; a disk scan covering TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET runs after the tailnet step and before isolation; both disk scans and redact-check include TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET; the isolation step fails closed if ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN is present in its environment; the decision record is corrected (redaction is accident hygiene, not a control; the request token is the runtime token; the OIDC acceptance is withdrawn).

Decision gates:
1. Before editing, confirm with gh secret list --env oracle (names only) that TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID and TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET exist. If not, set this item blocked with the owner setup steps and continue other items.
2. Confirm the pinned tailscale action supports oauth-secret with tags; if an upgrade is needed, pin the new version by full SHA and record why.
3. Read the action source at the pinned SHA and confirm it leaves no runner-user-readable copy of the secret or derived auth key; if it does, add that path to both disk scans before merging. Also inventory, read-only, the hosted runner's credential files (.credentials*, _diag) for the secret or a derived key.
4. Residual (owner accepted 2026-10-26): the corrected decision record states that the reviewer can read and encode-leak OMP_GATEWAY_TOKEN and the gateway URL, and that the owner accepted this with compensating controls: the tag:oracle-ci ACL (gateway port, tailnet-only reachability), model scope, per-client quota and revoke.
